name: Match-number tokens for knockout traceability
summary:
Surface the FIFA match number on knockout matches only, using one consistent token form (the word MATCH followed by the number) as an uppercase, tracked, tabular-numeral micro-label that fits the Swiss theme without spending the red accent.

CORE DECISION (bracket traceability): give every knockout bracket card a HEADER STRIP whose left side is the card's own number token ('MATCH 89'). That token is the visual anchor. The next column's slot already reads 'Winner of match 89' (via resolveSlot), so the eye scans left, finds the card literally headed 'MATCH 89', and the link is explicit and symmetric: same word, same number, one a header and the other a slot sentence. The header is the cleanest spot because it sits structurally apart from the two team slots and reads as a caption for the whole card. The existing date/venue meta stays as the FOOTER, so the number (top) and logistics (bottom) bracket the slots.

TABLE: the number rides in the SAME stage cell, appended after .stage-tag as a separate lighter token ('ROUND OF 16  M89'). Group matches get nothing (guarded by !m.isGroup && m.num!=null). Short 'M89' in the dense table to save width; full 'MATCH 89' on the roomy bracket card and detail panel.

DETAIL PANEL: add a dedicated 'Match no.' fact row (knockout only).

All three sites share one CSS class family (.mno) so the token looks identical everywhere; no red is used; tabular-nums + uppercase tracking per the type system; AA-legible as --muted on --panel/transparent in both light and dark themes.

tableView.placement: Inside the existing stage cell of the Matches table row (index.html line 810), appended AFTER the .stage-tag span. Short 'M{num}' form to conserve column width. Knockout-only via !m.isGroup && m.num!=null.
tableView.markup: REPLACE line 810: ${esc(m.isGroup?m.group:m.round)} WITH: ${esc(m.isGroup?m.group:m.round)}${!m.isGroup&&m.num!=null?`M${m.num}`:""} Result for a Round-of-16 match: [ROUND OF 16] M89 (stage-tag is the existing outlined box; mno is a borderless muted token sitting just to its right). Group rows are unchanged.

bracketView.placement: matchCardHTML (index.html lines 998-1004). Add a HEADER strip as the first child of .bk-match (before trophy/slots) carrying the card's own number 'MATCH {num}'. Keep the existing .bk-meta footer (date/venue) exactly as is. All knockout cards have m.num, but guard anyway.

detailView.placement: matchDetailHTML facts <dl> (index.html line 869). Add a 'Match no.' row immediately AFTER the existing Stage row, knockout-only. Full plain integer (no 'M' prefix) since space is ample and it reads as a stated fact.

rationale: One token, three sites: a single .mno class keeps 'match number' visually identical wherever it appears, which is exactly what makes the bracket traceable — the brain learns the token once. The bracket card gains a dedicated header strip so its own number is the most prominent caption on the card (ink, top-left), directly mirroring the 'Winner of match N' sentence that resolveSlot already prints in the next column; the reader scans one column right, reads 'Winner of match 89', glances back and the source card is literally headed 'MATCH 89'. Putting the number in the header (not the footer) separates identity (who am I) from logistics (when/where), and right-aligning the round name in that same strip lets each card self-describe stage + number without a second row. In the table the number is appended to the existing stage cell rather than adding a column, so layout is untouched and group rows are unaffected; the short 'M89' form conserves the dense grid while 'MATCH 89' is spelled out where there is room. All choices honour the theme: monochrome (muted in secondary contexts, ink only for the card's own primary number), square, hairline rule, uppercase tracking, tabular-nums, and zero use of the red accent which is reserved for meaning.
pros:
- Single reusable .mno token — consistent, low-code, easy to maintain.
- Bracket header makes 'MATCH 89' the card's anchor, directly matching 'Winner of match 89' in the next column — strong traceability.
- No new table column; group rows untouched; knockout-only guards are explicit.
- Fully on-theme: monochrome, square, hairline, uppercase/tracked, tabular-nums; no red spent.
- Header also surfaces the round name per card, a small bonus for orientation.
- AA-legible in both themes (--muted/--ink on --panel).
cons:
- Adds one row of height to every bracket card (the header strip); on very dense bracket layouts this costs vertical space — mitigated by tight --sp-1 padding.
- Two token forms ('M89' in table vs 'MATCH 89' elsewhere) is a minor inconsistency, accepted as a density tradeoff; could be unified to 'MATCH 89' everywhere if table width allows.
- The card header and the existing .bk-meta footer both add chrome; cards now have header + 2 slots + footer (4 bands). If that feels heavy, the round name could be dropped from the header.
- Match numbers are FIFA-specific jargon; the title="FIFA match number" tooltip and the explicit detail-panel row are the only affordances explaining them.
